$comment: The structured block of a target's THREAT_MODEL.md (plan step I7): a fenced code block whose info string is `framac-threat-model` (or `json framac-threat-model`) holding one JSON object. scripts/trust.py reads it. A function is named `name` or `file#name` (file relative to the target root); `unit` is a link unit of the build capture, by its full name or its file name (`build/libfoo.a` or `libfoo.a`). The four lists are required and may be empty: an empty list states that the target has none. `assets`, `invariants` and `call_rules` are optional.

lvalue.$comment: a C lvalue: a global (`config`, `session.mode`) or a field reached from a parameter (`ctx->mode`)

predicate.$comment: an ACSL predicate written into a generated annotation, like secrets[].size: no comment delimiter (`/*`, `*/`, `//`), no `;`, and none of `\result` (MetAcsl refuses it in a postcondition and turns it into a silent \true under \tguard), `\flags`, `proof:` (proof:deduce and proof:axiom assume the property instead of checking it), `\tguard`, `\inter`, `\in_file`

input_sources.$comment: Where attacker-controlled data enters. role `entry`: the function's parameters (the ones in `params`, or all) carry attacker data, so it is an untrusted entry point. role `reader`: the function returns or fills attacker data for its caller, like read(2); its callers and everything they reach are on the input path. A reader may be an external function (not defined in the target).

trusted_callers.$comment: Functions only trusted code calls: their preconditions may constrain values, and they are not untrusted entry points even when the library exports them. Either a `unit` (its API, minus `except`) or a list of `functions`.

secrets.$comment: Data that must not leak and must be wiped (security layer L6, step I9).

kind.$comment: local (plan step M6): an array local of `function`, wiped before each return in its scope

function.$comment: where the secret is released (kind global) or held (parameter, field, local): its wipe is checked when this function returns (step I9)

size.$comment: step I9: number of elements to wipe, a C expression over constants and the function's parameters (`len`, `32`); default sizeof for arrays. It is written into a generated annotation, so it cannot hold a comment delimiter (`/*`, `*/`, `//`)

object.$comment: step I9, kind field: the parameter or global holding the field

auth_gates.$comment: Checks that must pass before privileged functions run (security layer L4, step I9).

success.$comment: plan step M7: the value the gate returns when the check passed (a C constant expression: `0`, `1`, `AUTH_OK`); any other result must leave `state` unchanged

output_sinks.$comment: Where the target's output leaves it (security layer L5, step I9).

params.$comment: step I9: the parameters carrying the output (default: the pointer parameters)

length.$comment: step I9: the parameter giving the number of elements `params` point to

format.$comment: plan step M5: the parameter holding a printf-style format; every call must pass a string literal there (CWE-134)

checked_at.$comment: a wrapper sink: the function completes the buffer itself (a header length, a checksum) and then hands it to these sinks, each declared in this list too. L5 is then checked inside the wrapper, before each call that hands the buffer on, instead of at the wrapper's callers. Only for a sink the target defines whose property is initialized bytes (not kind log, terminal or buffer). security_props.py checks the claim against the model and keeps the property at the callers when it does not hold

assets.$comment: Optional (docs/plans/metacsl-exploitation-plan.md, package D1). Data only some functions may write, and optionally only some may read (security layer L3, class l3_isolation): properties L3_writers_<name> and L3_readers_<name>. An absent list states nothing.

params.$comment: for an lvalue reached from a parameter: the other parameter names the object is passed as (`s` when helpers take `struct conf *s`). A function that takes it under a name not listed here is not checked

writers.$comment: the functions allowed to write it; empty: nothing in the target writes it

readers.$comment: the functions allowed to read it; absent: reads are not restricted

invariants.$comment: Optional (package D1). A predicate over globals that the functions in `scope` keep (security layer L4, class l4_invariant): property L4_invariant_<name>. variant `weak`: at their boundaries (their callers must establish it at each call); `strong`: also after each write; `conditional`: kept when it holds on entry, nothing asked of the callers (entry points; `scope` required); `monotonic`: `lvalue` only moves `direction` (up: never decreases), at every write, and takes no `predicate`.

scope.$comment: the functions that keep it; absent: every function of the build (not for `conditional`)

call_rules.$comment: Optional (package D1). A predicate that holds at every call of `function`, defined or only declared (security layer L4, class l4_call_rule): property L4_call_<function>. The predicate names globals and the callee's parameters (the arguments of each call).
